messages.subject: Issue in dcat
parts:
Hi everyone,

In the attached two files, I have two models, one with a spatial component and one without a spatial component.

I would like to do the clustering in both cases, so I used the build function provided by the nimble "stick_breaking"

I noticed that the  zlatent  in the code fed correctly in the case of non-spatial, and the clusters start from 1, while I got a weird behaviour in the spatial one. The zlatent changes dramatically and is not drawn from dcat function properly.

The generation of   zlatent   in both cases should not depend on $i$


 zlatent[1:M] <- stick_breaking(vlatent[1:(M - 1)])
 
  for (j in 1:(M - 1)) {
    vlatent[j] ~ dbeta(1, alpha)
  }
 
  alpha ~ dgamma(1, 1)

Could you please clarify the strange behaviour of zlatent and dcat in spatial case that I obtained?

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: Issue in dcat
parts:
Hi Suzy,

Something of a side note, but the spatial code you sent won't run because in one place you have "latent[i]" and in another you have "latent[1,i]", which are inconsistent in terms of dimensionality. Same thing for "zlatent".

Once I fixed that, I can reproduce the strange behavior. I see that all the columns of your 'y' matrix are the same. I'm not sure what you intended, but that is presumably causing strange sampling behavior as you don't have information in your data to do the clustering that you seem to want to do.

-Chris

}

zlatent[1:M] <- stick_breaking(vlatent[1:(M - 1)])

}

alpha ~ dgamma(1,1)

})

                      netdist$Latitude),ncol=2)

colnames(my_points) <- c("longitude", "latitude")

my_points

df <- my_points
dist_mat <- pdist(df)
dist_1 <- pdist(df[, 1])
dist_2 <- pdist(df[, 2])

dist_prod <- product_metric(dist_1, dist_2)
# check equality

Data <- list(y = y, x1 = x1, x2 = x2, x3 = x3, x4 = x4, x5 = x5,
                Dist = dist_prod)
Const <- list(S = S, M = 50, N = N, D = 50)

Inits <- list(psi_y = rep(1, Const$S), lambda = 10,alpha=1,
                 latent = sample(1:50, size = Const$S, replace = TRUE), tau_bm = 1,  mu_bm = rnorm(5), phi = 1,
                 vlatent = rbeta(Const$M - 1, 1, 1),bm=matrix(rnorm(320),nrow = 64,ncol = 5))

mcmc<- nimbleMCMC(code = Code, data = Data, constants = Const,
                       inits = GWRInits, niter = 5000, nchains = 1,
                       monitors = c("latent", "lambda",'b','bm'), setSeed = TRUE)


So, is there any suggestion to solve the weird behaviour for doing the clustering ( I am interested to do the clustering for betas)

Thanks in advance.

Regards,
Suzy

messages.subject: Re: Issue in dcat
parts:
HI Suzy,

This is getting somewhat beyond the scope of the help that the development team can provide (though others on the list are always welcome to make suggestions).

Here are a few thoughts that might be helpful to you as you think further about your model.

In a standard clustering application, one might have `n` observations or random effects and want to cluster them. So you'd have code like:

y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], sd = sigma)    
mu[i] <- mu_cluster[latent[i]]
latent[i] ~ dcat( .... )
....

Or you might cluster regression coefficients, e.g.,
y[i] ~ dnorm(b0[i] + b1[i]*x[i], sd = sigma)
b0[i] <- b0_cluster[latent[i]]
b1[i] <- b1_cluster[latent[i]]

So there is a latent[i] for each observation. In your case you seem to have a single (multivariate) Y[1:N] vector so I don't see where you have
multiple things that you want to create clusters out of. I.e., if you remove the redundant columns of Y, you have:
mu_y[1:N] <- b[1]*x1[1:N] + b[2]*x2[1:N] + ...
and you have 5 'b' coefficients. It's not clear to me what you're trying to do, but my suggestion is to see if you can make an analogy to that simple clustering context for your problem setting.

-chris
